items.note: Within-subjects study (N = 35) of the Alternative Uses Task under flexible AI, persistent AI, and no-AI conditions, with originality scored; order randomization not stated in the abstract, and N is below 50.

Mixed-methods experiment with 41 product-design students comparing unaided, Internet-assisted, and GenAI-assisted ideation, with creativity of design outcomes scored; assignment and within/between design not stated, and N is below 50.
Single-factor between-subjects experiment with 113 college students using Kimi AI versus a comparison, with creativity scored on an alien-drawing task; random assignment not stated.

Quasi-experiment with 230 Chinese university students in human-ChatGPT, human-Google, and human-human dyad groups on a mathematical creativity task, scoring fluency, flexibility, and originality; non-random assignment, so it may move to observational context.

Five-day between-subjects classroom study (N = 38, ages 7 to 11) comparing curriculum only with curriculum plus an LLM agent, with divergent-thinking fluency, flexibility, and originality measured pre and post (likely after_ai); assignment not stated and N is below 50.

Experiment with 78 primary school students assigned to GenAI-supported (n = 20), peer-collaborative (19 pairs), or individual writing, with creative writing performance scored; assignment method not stated and the AI arm has only 20 students.
Systematic review of 27 empirical and theoretical studies (January 2022 to March 2024) on generative AI and creativity in education, focused on art and design; no pooled estimate in the abstract.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect all failed); title suggests a firm-level observational study of GenAI and innovation quantity versus quality (likely patents), and it may be out if the outcome is not novelty or originality.

Randomized experiment (N = 486, replication N = 640) comparing human-led and model-led LLM co-creation modes on idea quality, idea diversity, and perceived ownership; same study as arXiv 2510.23324, and the abstract does not mention the no-AI arm the search notes describe.

Pre-registered analysis of 4,820 psychology lab reports by 2,000 undergraduates (2016 to 2025), measuring style (including lexical diversity), sentiment, and grades before and after ChatGPT's release, with reports growing more similar to GPT text.
